note: Five symmetric bins applied to what the forecaster asserts. A denial of E takes 1 minus the bin value. A stated number overrides the map (a range takes its midpoint; 'at least x' takes x). A qualified phrase around a number ('substantially more than 50/50') is a phrase and takes the qualifier's bin. The strongest phrase in the claim sentence decides; coders never read tone.
sources: Lichtenstein S, Newman JR (1967). Empirical scaling of common verbal phrases associated with numerical probabilities. Psychonomic Science 9:563-564.
Kent S (1964). Words of estimative probability. Studies in Intelligence 8(4).
Budescu DV, Broomell S, Por HH (2009). Improving communication of uncertainty in the reports of the IPCC. Psychological Science 20:299-308.
Reagan RT, Mosteller F, Youtz C (1989). Quantitative meanings of verbal probability expressions. Journal of Applied Psychology 74:433-442.
Wallsten TS, Budescu DV, Rapoport A, Zwick R, Forsyth B (1986). Measuring the vague meanings of probability terms. JEP: General 115:348-365.
